claim_text: A differentiation ordering exists among dNK1 / dNK2 / dNK3

audit.primary_source_citation: Guo C, Cai P, Jin L, Sha Q, Yu Q, Zhang W, et al. Single-cell profiling of the human decidual immune microenvironment in patients with recurrent pregnancy loss. Cell Discov. 2021;7:1. doi:10.1038/s41421-020-00236-z. PMID 33390590 / PMC7779601. — NOTE: this is NOT the paper named in the hint. The hinted origin, Vento-Tormo R et al., Nature 2018;563:347-353 (PMID 30429548 / PMC7612850, doi:10.1038/s41586-018-0698-6), DEFINED dNK1/2/3 but makes no ordering claim whatsoever. Secondary ordering claims: Huhn O et al., Nat Commun 2020;11:381 (PMID 31959757/PMC6971012); Wang F et al., Genomics Proteomics Bioinformatics 2021;19:208-222 (PMID 33482359/PMC8602400).
audit.what_was_measured: In humans, in first-trimester decidua (mean 7.24 gestational weeks in controls, 8.50 in RPL) obtained at elective termination (controls) or by D&C after ultrasound-diagnosed embryo demise (RPL), CD45+ leukocytes were dissociated and profiled by 10x scRNA-seq in 24 women (15 control, 9 RPL), yielding 9,409 dNK cells; dNK1/dNK2/dNK3/dNKp were assigned by Seurat marker-gene clustering (CD39+CD18-CD103- / CD18+CD103-CD39- / CD18+CD103+CD39- / proliferating), and Palantir diffusion-based pseudotime plus velocyto RNA velocity were then computed OVER THAT SAME EMBEDDING to infer branch order. Subset proportions were re-measured by flow cytometry in an additional 23-24 women per arm. The only non-computational test of conversion: sorted CD39-CD18- dNK cells were cultured 2 days in vitro and re-stained for CD39, in 5 independent experiments. ATAC-seq of sorted dNK1/2/3 was run on a separate, unspecified cohort. In the hinted origin paper (Vento-Tormo 2018), at 6-14 gestational weeks in 11 deciduas / 5 placentas / 6 matched blood donors, dNK1/2/3 were defined ONLY by Seurat shared-nearest-neighbour graph clustering plus marker z-scores, confirmed by flow cytometry in 6 deciduas, KIR typing in 5 deciduas and Giemsa morphology in 2 replicates; NO trajectory analysis of any kind was run on dNK cells there.
audit.n: 24 women for scRNA-seq (15 control, 9 RPL); 43-47 women for flow-cytometry proportion validation (n_c=20-24, n_p=23-24); 5 independent experiments for the in vitro CD39 conversion assay (donor count not stated); ATAC-seq cohort size not stated. For Vento-Tormo 2018: 11 deciduas, 5 placentas, 6 blood donors.
audit.n_unit: women / first-trimester decidual donors (NOT cells; the 9,409 dNK figure is a cell count and is not an independent-replicate n). In vitro assay n_unit = independent experiments.
audit.controls: Healthy first-trimester elective-termination deciduas as comparison arm (n=15 scRNA-seq, n=20-24 flow); integration against the independent Vento-Tormo 2018 healthy reference dataset to test which paths reproduce; orthogonal Smart-seq2 confirmation of Path T cells; flow-cytometry confirmation of subset proportions in a larger cohort. MISSING for the load-bearing conversion claim: no post-sort purity re-check reported for the CD39-CD18- fraction, no proliferation/CFSE or dye-dilution control to separate outgrowth from conversion, no clonal barcoding, no time-zero-matched unstimulated control for culture-induced CD39 induction, and no lineage tracing. Palantir root was not an observed cell but an imputed pseudo-cell built from the mean expression of dNKp — i.e. "progenitor first" was assumed, not measured.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: Two alternatives are each sufficient and neither is excluded. (1) MARKER INDUCTION, NOT LINEAGE CONVERSION: CD39/ENTPD1 is an activation-inducible ectonucleotidase. Sorted CD39-CD18- dNK cells acquiring CD39 over 2 days in culture is fully explained by activation-induced upregulation of a single marker on the SAME cells — a state change of the readout, not conversion into "dNK1", which is a multi-marker transcriptional identity (KIR-high, LILRB1+, granule-high, glycolytic) that was never re-measured after culture. Dissociation and culture are themselves known to induce activation programmes. (2) SELECTION/OUTGROWTH OF A PRE-EXISTING SUBSET (the canonical alternative): with no post-sort purity data and no proliferation control, preferential survival or expansion of a small CD39-dim contaminant already present at t=0 reproduces the result exactly. For the computational half, pseudotime and RNA velocity cannot distinguish "dNK2 becomes dNK1" from "dNK1 and dNK2 are independent, co-existing states that are adjacent in expression space"; Palantir's branch order is a deterministic consequence of the analyst-supplied root, which here was a synthetic dNKp pseudo-cell. Because dNK subsets are additionally documented to arise from at least three independent ontogenies (peripheral CD56bright recruitment via CXCL12, local CD34+ precursor commitment, CD56dim reprogramming), two-independent-origins is a live third explanation for transcriptome adjacency.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, and it is severe. (1) THE HINTED ORIGIN MAKES NO SUCH CLAIM. Vento-Tormo 2018 titles the section "Three decidual NK cell STATES" and its Methods state verbatim: "Only cells that were identified as trophoblast were considered for trajectory analysis." Monocle 2 was applied exclusively to trophoblast (EVT/SCT). There is no dNK pseudotime, no dNK velocity, and no developmental-order claim anywhere in that paper. The ordering is a later accretion, exactly as the hint suspected. (2) THE PUBLISHED ORDERINGS ARE MUTUALLY CONTRADICTORY IN DIRECTION. Wang et al. 2021 (Monocle3 + Slingshot) roots the trajectory in dNK1 and orders dNK1 -> dNK2 -> dNK3 -> dNK4, explicitly calling dNK1 IMMATURE (CD27-CD11b-, EOMES-high). Huhn et al. 2020 (CyTOF, protein) places dNK2 "along a differentiation trajectory between dNK3 and dNK1" with dNK1 as the KIR-acquired, granule-high MATURE endpoint — the exact opposite polarity for the same subset. Guo et al. 2021 recovers neither linear order: dNKp branches in PARALLEL into dNK1 (Path 1), dNK2 (Path 2) and dNK3 (Path 3), i.e. three sibling branches with no ordering among dNK1/2/3 at all. Three papers, three incompatible topologies, all from transcriptome/marker adjacency. (3) GUO'S OWN RESULTS UNDERCUT THE ORDERING: their RNA velocity recovered only dNKp -> dNK1 and dNK2, NOT dNK3; and Path 3 (the dNK3 branch) is stated to be "apparently RPL-specific," i.e. absent from the healthy integration — a disease-state feature, not a normal differentiation order. (4) GUO'S OWN STATED LIMITATION: RPL decidua were collected after fetal demise, so "some alterations of decidual immune cells we observed in this study could be the consequence of the fetal death." (5) THE ENTITIES BEING ORDERED ARE UNSTABLE: 3 subsets (Vento-Tormo), 5 (Wang, adding dNK4 "between dNK1 and dNK3"), and Huhn splits dNK3 into two clusters (c5, c8) — ordering is being asserted over objects that do not replicate across studies. (6) The 2026 review that propagates this claim (PMID 42212143) itself concedes: "pseudotime analyses are computational inferences based on transcriptomic snapshots and do not constitute direct evidence of cellular lineage relationships. Prospective lineage tracing would be required." (7) SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND: no human dNK lineage tracing, fate mapping, or clonal barcoding study exists in my searches — so no OBS_DIRECT, OBS_TRANSFER or OBS_GENETIC evidence anchors any ordering.
audit.downstream_dependency: CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCY: Guo et al. 2021's central disease model, the section literally titled "Aberrant differentiation trajectory impairs dNK1 cell subset accumulation in RPL patients" — the claim that recurrent pregnancy loss is caused by a BLOCKED dNK2-like -> dNK1 conversion (Path T cells falling from 10.97% in healthy decidua to 4.81% in RPL). If dNK1/dNK2/dNK3 are independent co-existing states rather than an ordered series, the reduced CD39-CD18- fraction in RPL is merely a composition shift, the word "impairs" is unsupported, and the paper's proposed therapeutic rationale (restoring dNK1 by promoting conversion) collapses. SECOND NAMED DEPENDENCY: Cheung et al. 2025 (bioRxiv) iPSC-derived decidual NK subtype protocol, which interprets TGF-beta as a "negative regulator of dNK3 differentiation" (42% dNK3 without TGF-beta vs 1% with) — reading that titration as movement along a differentiation ordering requires the ordering to be real. THIRD: Wang et al. 2021's assignment of dNK4 as a late/terminal state "between dNK1 and dNK3 on the differentiation trajectory." NOT dependent: the dNK1/2/3 subset definitions themselves and the entire marker/function/ligand-receptor literature built on them survive intact if the ordering is false, which is why this grades MEDIUM rather than HIGH.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: The BOTTOM LINE of Claude's call survives — this is pure inference, no observational evidence, weakest tier — but BOTH of its specifics are wrong, in opposite directions. (a) IT OVER-CREDITS THE ATTRIBUTION. "Pseudotime only" presupposes that the origin paper ran a pseudotime supporting an ordering. Vento-Tormo 2018 ran NO dNK trajectory at all; its Methods restrict Monocle 2 to trophoblast ("Only cells that were identified as trophoblast were considered for trajectory analysis") and it deliberately calls them "three decidual NK cell STATES." The claim is not in the primary source it is normally attributed to; it is a later accretion (Huhn 2020, Guo 2021, Wang 2021). An auditor grading this as "pseudotime in Vento-Tormo" would be grading a paper that does not contain the claim. (b) IT UNDER-CREDITS THE ACTUAL EVIDENCE CLASS. The real ordering literature is not pseudotime-only: Huhn 2020 supplies CyTOF PROTEIN marker intermediacy (Eomes/Tbet), which is INF_MARKER and independent of any pseudotime; and Guo 2021 supplies a 2-day in vitro conversion assay of sorted CD39-CD18- cells, which is INF_INVITRO — a strictly stronger class than INF_TRAJECTORY. So the strongest class is INF_INVITRO, not INF_TRAJECTORY. (c) A THIRD FINDING NEITHER CALL ANTICIPATED: the three published orderings are mutually contradictory in direction (Wang: dNK1 immature -> dNK3; Huhn: dNK3 -> dNK2 -> dNK1 mature; Guo: no ordering among them, three parallel branches from dNKp). The claim as stated — "a differentiation ordering exists among dNK1/dNK2/dNK3" — is therefore not merely weakly evidenced but not even consistently specified in the literature that asserts it. Per G7 I am not loosening this to make it interesting: the honest grade is that the ordering is unestablished and its direction is contested.
audit.methods_quote: Vento-Tormo 2018 (PMID 30429548), Methods, verbatim: "Only cells that were identified as trophoblast were considered for trajectory analysis. Trajectory modelling and pseudotemporal ordering of cells was performed with the monocle 2 R package (version 2.8.0)." And Results heading, verbatim: "Three decidual NK cell states" / "We identified three main dNK subsets (dNK1, dNK2 and dNK3), which all co-express the tissue-resident markers CD49A (also known as ITGA1) and CD9." || Guo 2021 (PMID 33390590), verbatim: "We applied a high-resolution pseudo-time prediction algorithm Palantir to construct the differentiation potential trajectory of all dNK cells... We found three developmental branches where dNKp differentiate into dNK1 cells (Path 1) and into two distinct branches of dNK2 and dNK3 cells (Path 2 and Path 3). We also identified a differentiation pathway wherein dNK2-like cells with an apparent tendency to transform into dNK1 cells (Path T)." And: "To accurately define the initial cell state, we imputed a pseudo cell as the start cell by calculating the average gene expression of our identified dNKp cells." And the in vitro assay legend: "Percentage of CD39+ dNK1 cells before and after CD39-CD18- NK cells cultured in vitro for 2 days... representative in five independent experiments." || Huhn 2020 (PMID 31959757), verbatim: "dNK2 express intermediate levels of both Eomes and Tbet suggesting that they might be positioned along a differentiation trajectory between dNK3 and dNK1." || Wang 2021 (PMID 33482359), verbatim: "the trajectory of the root cells in dNK1 sequentially passed through dNK2 cells with a complex series of branches and reunions, and further through dNK3 to dNK4 toward the end of trajectory."
audit.notes: HINT VERIFICATION: The hint's suspicion was correct and is confirmed against full text, not abstract. Vento-Tormo et al. Nature 2018 exists exactly as cited (PMID 30429548), did define dNK1/2/3, and does NOT claim any differentiation ordering among them. Retrieval note: lit.py methods returned ABSTRACT_ONLY for this PMID (author manuscript, EPMC isOpenAccess=N, fullTextXML empty) and direct curl to pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov was blocked by reCAPTCHA; full text was obtained as the 26-page EPMC author-manuscript PDF (europepmc.org/articles/PMC7612850?pdf=render) and text-extracted locally, so every Vento-Tormo quote above is from the actual manuscript body. Guo 2021, Huhn 2020 and Wang 2021 were retrieved as OA full text and archived (refs/S1_PMC7779601.txt, refs/S1_PMC6971012.txt, refs/S1_PMC7612850.txt). Working files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-aaa/5f46e874-56b9-5c6b-9d27-d08dbfb1d5d8/scratchpad/vt_flat.txt (Vento-Tormo full text), PMC7779601.txt (Guo), huhn.txt, PMC8602400.txt (Wang), dnk3rev.txt (2026 review). G5 COMPLIANCE: I have deliberately not reported the 9,409-dNK-cell figure as an n; the replicate unit is women. G2 COMPLIANCE: Palantir, Monocle3, Slingshot and velocyto results are all classed INF_TRAJECTORY regardless of the confident framing ("Aberrant developmental trajectory", "As expected, RNA velocity predicted..."). G3 COMPLIANCE: the absence of lineage-tracing evidence is a SEARCHED-AND-NOT-FOUND result across 10 searches, not an assumption. CAVEAT ON PROPAGATION PATH: the modern restatement of this claim traces through a 2026 Frontiers in Immunology review (PMID 42212143) which cites Guo as ref 18; that review is a secondary source and was used only to locate primary references, never as evidence. One source in that chain, Cheung et al. 2025, is a bioRxiv preprint (not peer reviewed) and I did not independently retrieve it.

adv.challenge_reason:
DOWNGRADE: INF_INVITRO -> INF_MARKER. I re-pulled the methods myself (lit.py methods 33390590, 31959757; archived refs/S1_recheck_PMC7779601.txt, refs/S1_recheck_PMC6971012.txt) and the auditor's upgrade does not survive the gating definitions in Guo's own paper.

(1) THE IN VITRO ASSAY DOES NOT TEST AN ORDERING AMONG dNK1/dNK2/dNK3. Guo's Methods, verbatim: "To characterize the 'Path T' cells, we sorted CD39-CD18- dNK cells, which we cultured in RPMI-1640 with 10% fetal bovine serum. After 2 days... We then performed FACS for the detection of CD39 and CD18 expression in cultured dNK cells." By Guo's OWN definitions in the same paper (Methods, ATAC sorting gates): dNK1 = CD39+CD103-CD18-, dNK2 = CD39-CD103-CD18+, dNK3 = CD39-CD103+CD18+. A CD39-CD18- sort therefore excludes dNK1 (CD39+) AND excludes both dNK2 and dNK3 (both CD18+). The sorted input is none of the three subsets the claim orders. The experiment shows at most X -> dNK1 where X is outside {dNK1,dNK2,dNK3}; it supplies zero in vitro evidence for an ordering AMONG the three. The auditor's own row reproduces this error, calling it a "dNK2-like -> dNK1 conversion" while simultaneously quoting the CD39-CD18- gate, without noticing that CD18-negative cannot be dNK2.

(2) THE ASSAY'S INPUT IS ITSELF A TRAJECTORY CONSTRUCT. "Path T" exists only as a Palantir output; CD39-CD18- was reverse-engineered as its flow proxy from the observation that Path T cells "expressed low levels of CD39 and CD18 genes." Per G2 a trajectory is never an observation, and running a culture on a population *defined by* a trajectory output does not launder the inference.

(3) THE PRODUCT IS SCORED ON ONE ACTIVATION-INDUCIBLE MARKER. Only CD39/CD18/CD103 were restained; no KIR, LILRB1, granule proteins or transcriptome. "dNK1" is a multi-marker identity; CD39 alone is not it. (Auditor correct here.) I also could NOT verify the "representative in five independent experiments" figure-legend quote in the OA full text I retrieved, and Guo's Methods state no replicate n for this assay and no n for the ATAC-seq cohort — so the auditor's n for the load-bearing experiment rests on a legend I could not confirm.

(4) THE OTHER IN VITRO SOURCE IS ALSO OFF-TARGET. The auditor's "Cheung et al. 2025 bioRxiv" is now peer-reviewed: Cheung VC et al., Stem Cells 2026, PMID 41999228 (preprint PMID 41279445). Abstract, verbatim: "treatment with TGFbeta enriched for dNK2 subtype, while inducing dNK markers, CD9 and CD103" and "changes in dNK function across gestation reflect shifts in dNK subtypes that can be reproducibly derived from iPSC." That is signal-instructed subtype composition from a pluripotent source - a parallel/branching result - not a test of whether dNK2 becomes dNK1. Note the auditor described this source from an unretrieved preprint and reported numbers ("42% dNK3 vs 1%") I cannot verify in the published abstract, which instead frames the effect as enrichment FOR dNK2.

(5) WHAT IS ACTUALLY STRONGEST, ON-CLAIM. Huhn 2020 (PMID 31959757): in humans, first-trimester decidua from elective terminations at 7-12 gestational weeks in n = 28 women (plus n = 4 blood donors), matched cryopreserved decidual mononuclear cells and PBMCs were stained with a 41-marker mass cytometry panel and clustered on a tSNE landscape; intracellular Eomes and T-bet protein were quantified per cluster. Results (measurement): "dNK1 (c10-c13) express the highest levels of Eomes, whilst dNK3 (c5, c8) preferentially express Tbet. In comparison, dNK2 expresses intermediate levels of both." That is protein-level marker intermediacy = INF_MARKER. The ordering itself appears only in the Discussion as a hedge: "suggesting that they might be positioned along a differentiation trajectory between dNK3 and dNK1." Exactly the G1 pattern - the methods measured marker intermediacy; the discussion supplied the lineage.

(6) NO OBS_* WAS MISSED IN THE SOURCES THE AUDITOR GRADED - but see new_counter_evidence: I found one paper (Strunz 2021) whose DESIGN is OBS_TRANSFER-class and whose full text I could not obtain, and one genuine OBS_GENETIC decidual fate-mapping study (mouse). Neither can raise this grade on what I was able to read, so the strongest class I can defend from methods I actually read is INF_MARKER.

(7) INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED AND UPHELD: the auditor's central hint-verification. From my own extraction of the Vento-Tormo author manuscript (scratchpad/vt_flat.txt), Methods verbatim: "Only cells that were identified as trophoblast were considered for trajectory analysis. Trajectory modelling and pseudotemporal ordering of cells was performed with the monocle 2 R package (version 2.8.0)." Results heading verbatim: "Three decidual NK cell states". I read the entire dNK results passage: it makes no ordering claim of any kind. Vento-Tormo 2018 is correctly excluded as the primary source.
adv.revised_evidence_type_strongest: INF_MARKER (strongest class that actually bears on an ordering among dNK1/dNK2/dNK3, from methods I read myself). ALL PRESENT, ranked: INF_MARKER (Huhn 2020 PMID 31959757 - CyTOF protein Eomes-int/Tbet-int in dNK2 vs Eomes-hi dNK1 and Tbet-hi dNK3, 41-marker panel, n = 28 first-trimester women); INF_TRAJECTORY (Guo 2021 PMID 33390590 Palantir + velocyto rooted on an imputed pseudo-cell built from mean dNKp expression; Wang 2021 PMID 33482359 Monocle3 + Slingshot; Strunz 2021 PMID 33617461 also ran pseudotime per its data-availability statement); INF_INVITRO (present in the literature but OFF-TARGET for this claim - Guo's CD39-CD18- 2-day culture sorts a population that is none of dNK1/2/3; Cheung 2026 PMID 41999228 iPSC-dNK TGFbeta skewing tests instruction, not ordering); INF_KINETIC (Whettlock 2022 PMID 35784314 cross-sectional subset proportions across seven reproductive-cycle stages - a composition time-course, no labelling, cannot separate conversion from differential recruitment/retention). NOT ESTABLISHED: no OBS_DIRECT, OBS_TRANSFER or OBS_GENETIC evidence for an ordering among the three human subsets that I could read at methods level. CONDITIONAL UPGRADE PATH, EXPLICITLY FLAGGED: Strunz et al., Sci Immunol 2021, PMID 33617461, is an OBS_TRANSFER-class design (MISTRG humanized mice; human uterus-transplantation cohort with Brannstrom as co-author; monozygotic twins from the Swedish Twin Registry; MeSH "Observational Study", "Longitudinal Studies") reporting "a differentiation pathway of uNK cells in vitro and in vivo with sequential acquisition of killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptors and CD39" - KIR and CD39 being precisely the dNK1-defining markers. I could NOT obtain its Methods (Science Immunology paywall, no PMC deposit, no author manuscript found; lit.py methods 33617461 returned ABSTRACT_ONLY). Per G1 I refuse to classify from its abstract. This is the single highest-priority retrieval gap in the row and could move the strongest class to OBS_TRANSFER if its methods show the design was applied to the dNK1/2/3 subsets rather than to a continuous KIR/CD39 axis.
adv.new_counter_evidence:
FIVE items the prior auditor did not report; the first two are the important ones.

(A) GENETIC FATE MAPPING IN DECIDUA EXISTS, AND IT FAVOURS THE CANONICAL ALTERNATIVE. Mohamed MA, Li Y, Wegrzynowicz AK, Lindner PN, Vazquez J, Lopez GE, Stanic AK. "T-bet Fate Mapping Reveals Gestational Stage-Specific Transcriptional Adaptation of Decidual NK Cells." Am J Reprod Immunol 2026;95(3):e70220. PMID 41782473 / PMC12961421 (archived refs/S1adv_fatemap_PMC12961421.txt). Methods: B6.Rosa26-loxP-STOP-RFP(tdTomato) x Tbx21-Cre mice, backcrossed >=8 generations, syngeneically mated; virgin uterus and decidua/placenta at GD6-18; flow cytometry, bulk RNA-seq of sorted fate-mapped cells, and scRNA-seq of CD45+Lin- decidua at GD13.5 and GD18.5 (n = 1 sample per timepoint for scRNA-seq); flow n = 3-5 animals per group across 5 independent experiments. Findings: RFP+ (T-bet-history) decidual NK progressively lose T-bet PROTEIN as gestation advances (p < 0.0001 at GD12-14 and GD16-18) while retaining Eomes; but body text verbatim: "this was not the case, with few, if any RFP+T-bet neg cells expressing RORgammat... Similarly, we show no evidence of ILC1-ILC2 transition, as GATA3 was not detected either amongst RFP+T-bet neg cells." Internal control: no T-bet loss in Peyer's patches from the same animals, "indicating that it is specific to decidua, and not a global change or processing artifact." Conclusion verbatim: "Rather than undergoing lineage diversion, dNK cells adapt to the decidual environment via transcriptional compensation and SUBSET REDISTRIBUTION during pregnancy." This is the exact structural experiment the human field has never run: when lineage history is actually tracked in decidua, a large marker change across gestation turns out to be a state adaptation without conversion, and the compositional shift is redistribution. Honest caveats I am not glossing: it is mouse, mouse decidua has no dNK1/2/3, and the paper's own Abstract-Results sentence ("altered their lineage identity towards ILC2 or ILC3 fate") contradicts its body and Conclusions - per G1 I take the body.

(B) HUHN'S CyTOF DESTROYS GUO'S ROOT. Guo's entire branch topology depends on dNKp being a progenitor: Methods verbatim, "To accurately define the initial cell state, we imputed a pseudo cell as the start cell by calculating the average gene expression of our identified dNKp cells." Huhn 2020 measured that population at protein level and concluded the opposite, verbatim: "based on their expression of moderate levels of KIR and NKG2A and low expression of CD117 and CD127, we believe the Ki-67+dNKp population represent a mixture of dNK cells, INCLUDING dNK1, that are dividing within decidual tissue." If dNKp is cycling mature dNK rather than a precursor pool, Guo's analyst-supplied root is wrong and every branch direction downstream of it is unsupported. The auditor noted the root was imputed but did not find the paper that contradicts the premise.

(C) THE SUBSET DEFINITIONS DO NOT CROSS-VALIDATE AT PROTEIN LEVEL. Huhn 2020, verbatim: "Previous authors have described three main dNK populations, defined by NKp44 and CD103 expression. We find these populations spread across our tSNE map suggesting these markers do not correlate directly with the subsets defined by CyTOF." An ordering is being asserted over objects whose marker definitions do not map onto each other.

(D) ALL THREE SUBSETS PRE-EXIST BEFORE PREGNANCY - the canonical alternative in its strongest form. Whettlock EM, Woon EV, Cuff AO, Browne B, Johnson MR, Male V, Front Immunol 2022;13:880438, PMID 35784314 / PMC9245422 (archived refs/S1adv_PMC9245422.txt): flow cytometry plus integration of published scRNA-seq across seven reproductive-cycle stages (scRNA-seq arms: proliferative n = 3, secretory n = 3, first trimester n = 5, second trimester n = 1, third trimester n = 3 donors). uNK1/2/3 are present in NON-PREGNANT endometrium; "uNK1 and uNK2 peak in the first trimester, but by the third trimester, the majority of uNK are uNK3." Feyaerts D et al. 2024 (PMID 38571943 / PMC10987737) reports, from the same paper's reading of Whettlock, that "the frequency of uNK1, uNK2, and uNK3 subsets did not significantly differ between menstrual, proliferative, and secretory phase." So the three subsets co-exist at stable proportions before any trophoblast contact, and the gestational shift is a composition change equally explained by differential recruitment, retention or survival of pre-existing subsets. Feyaerts' own interpretation of the endometrium-to-decidua change is repertoire adaptation of the SAME cells, verbatim: "decidual NK cell precursors change their NK cell receptor repertoire composition upon pregnancy" - and they note fetal HLA-C genotype does not affect dNK KIR expression whereas MATERNAL HLA-C does, which points to education/selection of pre-existing KIR+ cells rather than conversion.

(E) WANG'S OWN PAPER CONTAINS A TWO-INDEPENDENT-ORIGINS CLAIM, and the auditor mis-paraphrased it. I read the text (scratchpad/PMC8602400.txt). Wang does NOT place dNK4 "between dNK1 and dNK3"; verbatim: "the trajectory of the root cells in dNK1 sequentially passed through dNK2 cells with a complex series of branches and reunions, and further through dNK3 to dNK4 toward the end of trajectory," and separately, verbatim: "Distance between dNK3 and dNK4 cells indicated the probably alternative origin of CD49a-CD56+CD16+ dNK4 cells." dNK4 is at the END, and Wang itself proposes an independent origin for it.

CORRECTION AGAINST THE AUDITOR, IN THE AUDITOR'S DISFAVOUR ON RIGOUR (G7 cuts both ways - I am not inflating contradictions): the auditor's claim that Huhn and Wang have "the exact opposite polarity" overstates the record. Huhn's sentence, "positioned along a differentiation trajectory BETWEEN dNK3 and dNK1," specifies adjacency, not direction; Huhn never names an endpoint. Huhn in fact warns against importing the pbNK KIR-maturation logic to dNK, verbatim: "dNK are quite different because as KIR co-expression increases, we find dNK1 exhibit decreased responsiveness to stimulation by missing self." So Huhn and Wang AGREE on the linear adjacency dNK1-dNK2-dNK3 with dNK2 in the middle; the genuine topological conflict is Wang's linear chain versus Guo's three parallel branches from dNKp, plus an unspecified direction in Huhn and a direction (dNK1 late, via sequential KIR/CD39 acquisition) implied by Strunz 2021 that is opposite to Wang's dNK1-as-root. That is still fatal to the claim as stated, but it is a smaller set of contradictions than the auditor asserted.

Also verified by me, not assumed: the 2026 review PMID 42212143 self-limitation quote is genuine, verbatim: "However, pseudotime analyses are computational inferences based on transcriptomic snapshots and do not constitute direct evidence of cellular lineage relationships. Prospective lineage tracing would be required to demonstrate the proposed differentiation paths."
adv.crossfield_g4_findings:
The home field for "does a differentiation ordering exist among N marker-defined subsets of one lineage" is myeloid/T/ILC, and all three have settled versions of this exact question. Every one of them required a method that no dNK1/2/3 paper has used.

MYELOID - the closest structural analogue, same n=3 subsets, same species, and it was NOT settled by markers or pseudotime. Patel AA, Zhang Y, Fullerton JN, Boelen L, Rongvaux A, Maini AA, Bigley V, Flavell RA, Gilroy DW, Asquith B, Macallan D, Yona S. "The fate and lifespan of human monocyte subsets in steady state and systemic inflammation." J Exp Med 2017;214(7):1913-1923. PMID 28606987 / PMC5502436 (archived refs/S1advG4p_PMC5502436.txt). Their framing of the problem is verbatim the S1 problem: "it remains to be shown what, if any, relationships exist among the three principal human monocyte subsets." They answered it with (i) in vivo stable-isotope labelling in healthy human volunteers (20 males, 5 females) - deuterium-labelled glucose incorporating into the DNA backbone of dividing cells, with mathematical modelling of label appearance and disappearance per subset, fitted with and without an inter-subset delay term (Fig. S2, Tables S1-S2) to test sequence explicitly - and (ii) adoptive transfer of sorted human classical monocytes into MISTRG humanized mice with a sacrifice time-course. Marker intermediacy between CD14/CD16 subsets was never accepted as sufficient. Neither deuterium labelling nor transfer has been done for dNK1/2/3.

ILC - the field has a written standard, and the dNK papers meet only its first clause. Kotas ME et al. (eds) / "'Just one word, plastic!': Controversies and caveats in innate lymphoid cell plasticity." Front Immunol 2022, PMID 36052086 / PMC9427196 (archived refs/S1advG4_PMC9427196.txt). Section titled "Methodologies to ascertain ILC plasticity", verbatim: "to truly evaluate plasticity, there must be corroborative evidence that consists of techniques such as single-cell transcriptomic studies accompanied by LINEAGE TRACING, BARCODING AND EPIGENETIC ANALYSES." Their worked example (Bielecki et al. skin ILCs) is instructive precisely because scRNA-seq showed "a dense continuum of functional states" that could have been read as a trajectory, and the conversion claim was only accepted after IL-5 fate-mapping and IL-22-BFP/IL-17A-GFP reporter validation in vivo. Guo/Huhn/Wang supply the scRNA-seq/CyTOF clause and none of the others.

HEMATOPOIESIS - trajectory inference has been benchmarked against clonal ground truth and it fails at exactly the step S1 needs. Weinreb C, Rodriguez-Fraticelli A, Camargo FD, Klein AM. "Lineage tracing on transcriptional landscapes links state to fate during differentiation." Science 2020;367:eaaw3381. PMID 31974159 (archived refs/S1advG4_PMC7608074.txt; ABSTRACT_ONLY - Science author manuscript, so I quote the abstract and do not paraphrase its methods). Verbatim: "Analysis of sister cells also revealed cells to have intrinsic fate biases NOT DETECTABLE by single-cell RNA sequencing... we benchmarked computational methods of dynamic inference from single-cell snapshots, showing that fate choice occurs earlier than is detected by state-of-the-art algorithms." Its companion is a formal limit result: Weinreb C, Wolock S, Tusi BK, Socolovsky M, Klein AM, "Fundamental limits on dynamic inference from single-cell snapshots," PNAS 2018;115:E2467-E2476, PMID 29463712. Together these establish the general proposition G2 encodes: transcriptome adjacency underdetermines lineage, and expression-space neighbours can carry different fates.

CD8 T CELL - the memory-subset ordering required single-cell resolution transfer, not population marker relationships. Buchholz VR et al., "Disparate individual fates compose robust CD8+ T cell immunity," Science 2013;340:630-635, PMID 23493420 (already archived in this repo as refs/P1G4_23493420.txt from a sibling claim). Population-level marker relationships did not describe individual-cell fate; single-cell adoptive transfer/fate mapping did.

RNA VELOCITY SPECIFICALLY - Gorin G, Fang M, Chari T, Pachter L, "RNA velocity unraveled," PLoS Comput Biol 2022, PMID 36094956. I located this by title/EPMC only and did NOT read its methods, so I cite it as existing, not as evidence.

RECRUITMENT-VERSUS-RESIDENCY / TRM METHODOLOGY - and here the home-field method HAS been applied to the uterus, which is the auditor's largest miss. The TRM field settles origin with parabiosis (mouse) and transplant chimerism (human). The human uterine analogue exists: Strunz et al. Sci Immunol 2021 (PMID 33617461) studied "human uterus transplantation and monozygotic twins" and reports the uNK "niche could be replenished FROM CIRCULATION and that it was under genetic control," alongside MISTRG humanized-mouse engraftment. Replenishment from circulation is the recruitment arm of the recruitment-versus-conversion dichotomy and is a live alternative to any in-situ ordering. I could not obtain the Strunz methods (paywalled, no PMC), so I report its design, not its results, and I do not credit it as establishing anything. Separately I ALSO searched for bone-marrow-transplant endometrial chimerism resolving uNK subset origin and found only stromal/decidual-cell engraftment work (e.g. PMID 31513564; PMID 23103021 reports peripheral blood stem cell transplants do NOT result in endometrial stromal engraftment) - nothing resolving uNK1/2/3 origin. SEARCHED AND NOT FOUND, not assumed absent.

WHAT THE HOME FIELDS ESTABLISH THAT BEARS ON S1, in one line: every field that has resolved a subset-ordering question did so with in vivo isotope labelling, adoptive/congenic transfer, or genetic fate mapping/clonal barcoding; where snapshot inference has been benchmarked against clonal truth it mis-times or misses the fate decision; and in the one case where genetic fate mapping HAS been applied to decidua (Mohamed 2026), the answer was subset redistribution and marker adaptation WITHOUT lineage conversion - i.e. the canonical alternative won on its home turf.

adv.load_bearing_reason:
MEDIUM is right, but the auditor's dependency list needs one deletion, one correction and two additions, and the reasoning needs to be anchored differently.

SURVIVES AND IS THE STRONGEST NAMED DEPENDENCY - Guo et al. 2021 (PMID 33390590), the section literally titled "Aberrant differentiation trajectory impairs dNK1 cell subset accumulation in RPL patients," and its quantitative core: Path T cells fall from a mean 540/4923 (10.97%) in healthy decidua to 216/4486 (4.81%) in RPL, read as "a weaker tendency of cells transform into dNK1 cells." Verbatim from the paper: "Our discovery of this differentiation pathway illustrates a previously unknown source of pregnancy-promoting dNK1 cells in the decidua." If dNK1/2/3 are co-existing states rather than an ordered series, "impairs" and "source" are both unsupported, the RPL finding reduces to a composition shift, and the therapeutic rationale of restoring dNK1 by promoting conversion collapses. Note the dependency is even more fragile than the auditor said, because Guo's own integration found Path 3 (the dNK3 branch) to be "apparently RPL-specific" and its RNA velocity recovered only dNKp -> dNK1 and dNK2, not dNK3.

SURVIVES BUT MUST BE RESTATED - Wang et al. 2021 (PMID 33482359). The auditor wrote that Wang assigns dNK4 as "a late/terminal state 'between dNK1 and dNK3 on the differentiation trajectory'." That is not Wang's text. Wang places dNK4 at the END of the chain ("further through dNK3 to dNK4 toward the end of trajectory") and separately proposes an independent origin for it ("Distance between dNK3 and dNK4 cells indicated the probably alternative origin of CD49a-CD56+CD16+ dNK4 cells"). What is genuinely dependent in Wang is its maturity assignment: dNK1 is called the immature root on the strength of a CD27-/CD11b- flow phenotype interpreted "according to previous studies" - i.e. the mouse splenic NK four-stage CD27/CD11b maturation scheme imported wholesale into human decidual NK without validation. That whole maturity claim is load-bearing on the ordering and on a cross-species marker convention.

SHOULD BE DROPPED AS THE AUDITOR STATED IT - the "Cheung et al. 2025 bioRxiv" dependency. The auditor conceded not retrieving it. It is now peer-reviewed (Cheung VC et al., Stem Cells 2026, PMID 41999228) and its published framing does not require an ordering: TGFbeta "enriched for dNK2 subtype," and the paper's own conclusion is that gestational functional change "reflect[s] shifts in dNK subtypes." Enrichment/skewing of composition in a de novo iPSC differentiation is compatible with parallel instruction and does not presuppose dNK1->dNK2->dNK3. Counting it as a dependency inflates the load.

TWO ADDITIONS I VERIFIED. (1) The 2026 Frontiers in Immunology review PMID 42212143, whose entire organising frame is dNK3 as a state within a differentiation scheme in RPL, and which cites Guo as ref 18 - it propagates the ordering into review-level consensus even while conceding, verbatim, that "pseudotime analyses... do not constitute direct evidence of cellular lineage relationships. Prospective lineage tracing would be required." (2) Whettlock 2022 (PMID 35784314) and every paper reading the gestational uNK1 -> uNK3 proportion shift as maturation along a series: that reading is dependent, whereas the underlying proportion measurement is not.

WHY NOT HIGH: the dNK1/2/3 subset definitions, their markers, their spatial distribution (Wang's serial-section immunohistochemistry placing CD39+ dNK1 in decidual compacta and CD103+ dNK3 in distal compacta/spongiosa), the KIR/LILRB1-HLA-C/HLA-G interaction biology, the CyTOF functional hierarchy (dNK2/dNK3 out-produce dNK1 for XCL1 and chemokines), and the RPL/reproductive-failure association literature all stand intact if the ordering is false. The ordering is an interpretive layer on a robust taxonomy, not the taxonomy's foundation.

WHY NOT LOW: the ordering is the sole support for a named causal disease mechanism in a well-cited paper, it has already been absorbed into 2026 review-level framing, and it is being used to license a therapeutic rationale (restore dNK1 by promoting conversion). A claim that is decorative in most of its literature but load-bearing for a proposed intervention is MEDIUM, not LOW.
adv.better_primary_source:
TWO CHANGES.

(1) BETTER PRIMARY SOURCE FOR THE CLAIM AS STATED: Huhn O, Ivarsson MA, Gardner L, Hollinshead M, Stinchcombe JC, Chen P, Shreeve N, Chazara O, Farrell LE, Theorell J, Ivarsson MA, Sharkey AM, Colucci F, Moffett A, et al. "Distinctive phenotypes and functions of innate lymphoid cells in human decidua during early pregnancy." Nat Commun 2020;11:381. PMID 31959757 / PMC6971012. doi:10.1038/s41467-019-14123-z. Rationale: it is the EARLIEST paper to assert an ordering among dNK1/dNK2/dNK3 (January 2020, predating both Wang and Guo, January 2021), it is the only one whose ordering-relevant measurement is protein rather than transcriptome-derived (41-marker CyTOF, intracellular Eomes/T-bet, n = 28 first-trimester women at 7-12 weeks from elective terminations plus n = 4 blood donors), and unlike Guo it actually positions the three subsets relative to one another. The auditor's pick, Guo 2021, is a poor primary source for THIS claim precisely because its Palantir result does not order dNK1/2/3 relative to each other at all - it places them as three sibling branches off dNKp. Grading Guo as the primary source for "an ordering exists among dNK1/2/3" grades a paper whose own trajectory output declines to assert one. Caveat to carry forward: Huhn's ordering claim is a single hedged Discussion sentence ("suggesting that they MIGHT be positioned along a differentiation trajectory between dNK3 and dNK1"), direction unspecified, resting on a Results-section marker measurement. That is the true provenance of claim S1 - a hedged one-line gloss on a CyTOF intermediacy, subsequently hardened by citation.

(2) HIGHEST-PRIORITY UNRESOLVED SOURCE, WHICH THE PRIOR ROW MISSED ENTIRELY AND WHICH SHOULD BE RETRIEVED BEFORE THIS ROW IS FINALISED: Strunz B, Bister J, Jonsson H, Filipovic I, Crona-Guterstam Y, Kvedaraite E, Sleiers N, Dumitrescu B, Brannstrom M, Lentini A, Reinius B, Cornillet M, Willinger T, Gidlof S, Hamilton RS, Ivarsson MA, Bjorkstrom NK. "Continuous human uterine NK cell differentiation in response to endometrial regeneration and pregnancy." Sci Immunol 2021;6(56):eabb7800. PMID 33617461. doi:10.1126/sciimmunol.abb7800. This is the only human uNK paper I found whose design is OBS_TRANSFER-class - MISTRG humanized mice, a human uterus-transplantation cohort (Brannstrom, the Gothenburg programme, is a co-author), and monozygotic twins from the Swedish Twin Registry - and it reports "a differentiation pathway of uNK cells in vitro and in vivo with sequential acquisition of killer cell immunoglobulin-like receptors and CD39," i.e. an ordering along exactly the markers that define dNK1, with a direction (dNK1 late) opposite to Wang's dNK1-as-root. It also bears directly on the recruitment-versus-conversion alternative: "the uNK cell niche could be replenished from circulation and... was under genetic control." I could NOT obtain its Methods - Science Immunology paywall, no PMC deposit, no author manuscript located; lit.py methods 33617461 returned ABSTRACT_ONLY. Per G1 I have therefore reported its DESIGN from the abstract and article-page metadata and have refused to credit any of its results or to let it raise the evidence grade. Obtaining this full text is the single action most likely to change the classification of claim S1, in either direction: if its transplant/humanized-mouse work is applied to a continuous KIR/CD39 axis rather than to the discrete dNK1/2/3 subsets, the row stands at INF_MARKER; if it is applied to the subsets, the strongest class becomes OBS_TRANSFER. The prior auditor's flat assertion that "no OBS_DIRECT, OBS_TRANSFER or OBS_GENETIC evidence anchors any ordering" was, on my searches, an over-strong negative on both counts - Strunz 2021 exists in humans, and Mohamed 2026 (PMID 41782473) is genuine OBS_GENETIC fate mapping in decidua, albeit in mouse.
